item.title: Visa used Mythos to hunt for bugs in its own payment network, then open-sourced the harness that made it possible
item.description: Visa aimed Anthropic's Claude Mythos at the infrastructure behind billions of daily transactions, a network that spans more than 200 countries and territories, moves money in roughly 160 currencies, and connects nearly 5 billion payment credentials to more than 175 million merchant locations. The model stitched minor weaknesses deep in the stack into working exploit chains that would traditionally have surfaced only late in penetration testing. Rajat Taneja, Visa's president of technology, walked the VB Transform 2026 audience through what came next, including why Visa released the harness tha...

item.title: Risques pour la sécurité nationale | Washington interdit l’importation de robots humanoïdes fabriqués à l’étranger
item.description: Le gouvernement Trump a ajouté mardi à une liste de produits et de sociétés interdits d’importation aux États-Unis les robots humanoïdes et quadrupèdes, estimant qu’ils présentent « des risques inacceptables pour la sécurité nationale » du pays.

item.title: 50-year-old A-10 Thunderbolt II Warthog gets reprieve as BRRRRT act keeps it alive after Iran showdown
item.description: The BRRRRT Act seeks to slow A-10 retirements by restoring capabilities and tightening replacement requirements following recent operational missions.

item.title: T-Mobile outage: Some users report they couldnt connect to Starlink via T-Satellite
item.description: T-Mobile's T-Satellite with Starlink service wasn't the immediate fix some customers were hoping for during the Monday outage.

item.title: Bot-detection startup Spur nabs $200M from Insight

item.description: Recent PSN and Xbox Live outages show why Sony's move to end game discs in 2028 should worry gamers who value owning what they pay for.

item.title: Big Oil profits are soaring while extreme heatwaves scorch the planet this summer
item.description: Emissions from the largest oil companies were enough to cause to 1 in 4 heatwaves over the past two decades, according to a new analysis from Oxfam. This summer, millions of people have felt the dire consequences of climate change as they faced extreme, record-breaking heat. And the Big Oil companies fueling those heat waves are seeing their profits soar, a new analysis finds. ...
